MN-2025-HF3404.aiSummary: This law raises the penalty for pretending to be a peace officer, and it adds a new crime for doing that while carrying a firearm. It also adds tougher penalties if someone commits another crime while pretending to be an officer. In some cases, officers must give their agency name, last name, and ID number, and the law takes effect August 1, 2026.

MN-2025-SF5309.title: Department of Agriculture Office of Business Regulation and Land Ownership establishment

actions.text: Referred to Agriculture, Veterans, Broadband, and Rural Development

MN-2025-SF5309.aiSummary: The bill would create a new office in the Department of Agriculture to study farm business consolidation and farm land ownership in Minnesota. It would look at purchases of agricultural land by people, companies, churches, and other nonprofits, and would give advice to the agriculture commissioner. The office would also send a report every two years to lawmakers, and the bill would set aside money in fiscal year 2027 to start and run it.

MN-2025-HF5154.policyArea: Agriculture and Agriculture Department, Appropriations, State Agencies and Departments
MN-2025-HF5154.aiSummary: The bill would create a new office in the Department of Agriculture to look at agriculture business concentration and farm land buying trends in Minnesota. It would also require the office to send a report every two years to lawmakers who handle agriculture. The agriculture commissioner would appoint a director and hire staff, and the bill would set aside an unspecified amount of general fund money in fiscal year 2027 for the office.

MN-2025-HF4384.policyArea: Children-Child Abuse and Neglect, Children-Child Care and Facilities, Health and Health Department
MN-2025-HF4384.aiSummary: The bill would change Minnesota child care training rules on abusive head trauma, which is harm to a baby or young child from shaking. It would require the training to be interactive, not just reading or watching material. The rules would apply to child care center directors, staff, substitutes, volunteers, and some family child care workers, and the changes would take effect January 1, 2027.

Introduction and first reading, referred to Commerce Finance and Policy

MN-2025-HF4090.aiSummary: The bill would change prize and ticket limits for paddlewheel gambling in Minnesota. It would keep the top cash prize at $70, set the top fair market value for a merchandise prize at $200, and raise the highest ticket price from $2 to $5. It affects groups that run this type of lawful gambling and people who buy paddle tickets.

MN-2025-HF3579.title: Eggs allowed to be donated past their quality assurance date.

actions.text: Bills identical, SF substituted on General Register
Referred to Chief Clerk for comparison with SF3891
Introduction and first reading, referred to Agriculture Finance and Policy

MN-2025-HF3579.policyArea: Agriculture and Agriculture Department, Food and Nutrition
MN-2025-HF3579.aiSummary: The bill would let eggs be donated after their quality assurance date if they stay in their original pack, were already checked and graded, and are kept cold. Charitable food assistance programs could give out those eggs for up to 30 days after that date, with a label saying they are donated eggs and not for resale. It also keeps the current rule that retail eggs must be removed from sale after set time limits based on the pack date.

MN-2025-HF2354.aiSummary: The bill would add a new crime for medical assistance fraud and update state law on how it is handled. It would give the attorney general more power to subpoena records tied to medical assistance fraud cases, including phone, banking, insurance, and wage records.
